headline: Neymar on bench as Brazil faces Scotland in World Cup Group C clash
summary: Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti makes one change to the lineup, with Rayan replacing the injured Raphinha.
details: Brazil faces Scotland in their final World Cup Group C match. Manager Carlo Ancelotti has made one change to the squad that previously defeated Haiti 3-0.
Forward Rayan has been brought into the starting lineup to replace the injured winger Raphinha. Rayan will lead the attack alongside Vinicius Jr and Matheus Cunha.
Neymar starts the game on the bench. This is the first match he has been fit to feature in during the World Cup after recovering from a calf injury sustained over a month ago.
Scotland coach Steve Clarke has made four changes to his side following a 1-0 loss to Morocco. New starters include Ben Gannon-Doak, Lawrence Shankland, Kenny McLean, and Scott McKenna.
The Brazil starting XI features Alisson, Danilo, Gabriel Magalhaes, Marquinhos, Douglas Santos, Casemiro, Bruno Guimaraes, Lucas Paqueta, Rayan, Vinicius Jr, and Matheus Cunha.
caption:
Neymar is back and fit, but he starts on the bench for Brazil's final Group C clash against Scotland!

Brazil faces Scotland in their final World Cup Group C match. Manager Carlo Ancelotti has made one change to the squad that previously defeated Haiti 3-0.

Forward Rayan has been brought into the starting lineup to replace the injured winger Raphinha. Rayan will lead the attack alongside Vinicius Jr and Matheus Cunha.

Neymar starts the game on the bench. This is the first match he has been fit to feature in during the World Cup after recovering from a calf injury sustained over a month ago.

Scotland coach Steve Clarke has made four changes to his side following a 1-0 loss to Morocco. New starters include Ben Gannon-Doak, Lawrence Shankland, Kenny McLean, and Scott McKenna.

The Brazil starting XI features Alisson, Danilo, Gabriel Magalhaes, Marquinhos, Douglas Santos, Casemiro, Bruno Guimaraes, Lucas Paqueta, Rayan, Vinicius Jr, and Matheus Cunha.

headline_marked: Bosnia beats Qatar 3-1, [[on verge of reaching World Cup knockout stages]]
headline: Bosnia beats Qatar 3-1, on verge of reaching World Cup knockout stages
summary: A victory over the 2022 hosts puts Bosnia-Herzegovina in a strong position to advance to the last 32 as Qatar exits the tournament.
details: Bosnia-Herzegovina defeated 2022 hosts Qatar 3-1 in their final Group B match, moving onto four points and putting them in a strong position to reach the knockout stages for the first time.
The match began with Bosnia dominating, leading to a goal from 18-year-old Kerim Alajbegovic, the youngest ever World Cup player for Bosnia, who scored a screamer from outside the area.
A second goal followed shortly after when a shot from 40-year-old talisman Edin Dzeko, winning his 150th cap, took a deflection off Qatar's defense and the goalkeeper to enter the net.
Qatar attempted a comeback when 35-year-old Hassan al-Haydos scored late in the first half, but the Qatari effort was hampered when al-Haydos left the pitch injured in the 55th minute.
Bosnia sealed the victory in the 80th minute when Ermin Mahmic scored his second goal in two successive matches, ending Qatar's World Cup dream.
caption:
Bosnia-Herzegovina is on the brink of its first-ever World Cup knockout stage appearance after a 3-1 win over Qatar.

Bosnia-Herzegovina defeated 2022 hosts Qatar 3-1 in their final Group B match, moving onto four points and putting them in a strong position to reach the knockout stages for the first time.

The match began with Bosnia dominating, leading to a goal from 18-year-old Kerim Alajbegovic, the youngest ever World Cup player for Bosnia, who scored a screamer from outside the area.

A second goal followed shortly after when a shot from 40-year-old talisman Edin Dzeko, winning his 150th cap, took a deflection off Qatar's defense and the goalkeeper to enter the net.

Qatar attempted a comeback when 35-year-old Hassan al-Haydos scored late in the first half, but the Qatari effort was hampered when al-Haydos left the pitch injured in the 55th minute.

Bosnia sealed the victory in the 80th minute when Ermin Mahmic scored his second goal in two successive matches, ending Qatar's World Cup dream.
